_note: The assistant engine's routes. The service answers seven of them today, exactly as apps/assistant-api/src/server.ts registers them: GET /assistant/health and one turn at POST /assistant/turn, and at the plan's own versioned addresses POST /assistant/v1/turn, POST /assistant/v1/knowledge/search, GET /assistant/v1/status and push-to-talk's two — POST /assistant/v1/listen and POST /assistant/v1/speak, built on 22 September 2026 against Azure Speech. The rest of the /v1/* family — triage conducted over Clinical's rules, a reading written through the Passport gateway, handover prepare and submit — is declared and not built: the engine's not-yet-available refusal answers each of them with 501, so a caller meets a sentence it can read rather than a 404 it cannot tell from a typo, and packages/mock-api answers them on loopback with synthetic data until each is built. Those five routes were re-declared at version two because that refusal's answeredBy now names them, and adding a refusal is a change as much as rewording one: each version one is withdrawn in its favour, with no callers, its shape and its refusals unchanged. listen and speak are at version three for the same kind of reason: the shape a built capture arrives in is audio rather than the captureMs window version two was frozen with, so their version two entries are withdrawn in version three's favour with no callers, and the engine's cloud-speech refusal, added with them, answers version three alone. /v1/knowledge/search is at version two for the same reason, with the three refusals its handler actually answers and its sources now declared as objects rather than as text; its version one is withdrawn in the same way. The turn's declared shape is this contract's reading of the service it captures; the service's own request type also accepts an optional visitId, and this contract refuses that name — another engine's resource under an Id name, per packages/catalog/apis.json#_contractIdsNote — so it is not declared here.

refusals.statement: A public model answers only where its activation was acknowledged.
refusals.why: The production acknowledgement gate of apps/assistant-api/src/lib/activation.ts: with a provider configured in production, the service refuses to start until the acknowledgement line is in its environment. A tier whose own gate could be skipped without the contract saying so would be a gate the contract never held.

refusals.statement: GilbertOne answers; it decides no clinical question.
refusals.why: The engine's own card in packages/catalog/events.json: it answers, and it decides no clinical question. A route in this file that could be read as deciding one is refused by this refusal before it is built.

refusals.statement: This route is not built yet, and it says so rather than pretending.
refusals.why: The plan's /v1 family was written ahead of the service that answers it, and every address it declares answers today: a turn, a knowledge search, the versioned status and push-to-talk's two, built on 22 September 2026, and the two triage steps, the vitals reading and the two handover steps, built later the same day. No route of this engine is refused with this sentence now, and the branch in apps/assistant-api/src/server.ts that reads it is kept for the next address this contract declares ahead of the handler that answers it — a declared route with no handler would otherwise fall to the 404 the server keeps for addresses it has never heard of, which a caller cannot tell from a typo. The version two entries this refusal names are the ones it answered while those five were unbuilt; each is withdrawn in favour of a built version three and each keeps this refusal naming it, so the sentence a caller met at the time is still the sentence on record. listen and speak left the list the day they were built, and the version two entries this refusal once answered for them were withdrawn in favour of version three.

refusals.statement: Cloud speech is not configured here; the browser's own voice is the one to carry on with.
refusals.why: Push-to-talk's two built addresses reach Azure Speech only when AZURE_SPEECH_KEY and AZURE_SPEECH_REGION are both set, read in apps/assistant-api/src/lib/speech.ts. Without them the routes answer this refusal rather than reaching for a service that is not there, and the web panel hears and speaks through the browser either way — so the caller is told which of the two voices is carrying it rather than given a failure. The sentence is read from this contract by the service, like every engine refusal, so it lives in one place.

refusals.statement: Guided triage is not clinically validated here, and it is refused rather than guessed.
refusals.why: Taking a person through assessment questions and setting a priority for them is a clinical act, and packages/catalog/clinical.json runs it only under a triage protocol the clinical governance board has ratified. Its triage.triageProtocols.ids names none, no protocol in packages/catalog/protocols.json is ratified, the board is not formed and no Medical Director is appointed, so apps/assistant-api/src/lib/triage-gate.ts reads the register and answers that the gate is shut. Both triage addresses are built and refuse with this sentence at a 503 rather than a 501: the routes exist and the clinical act does not, and a caller is told which. The gate reads the register and not a flag in code, so the board ratifying a protocol is what opens it, with no edit to a handler; the questions themselves are that protocol's own content, which no contract holds yet, and software guesses none of it. The sentence is read from this contract by the service, like every engine refusal, so it lives in one place.
